Many hosters download without JDownloader, the browser extension puts a download button on videos, KnightLoader comes as a Flatpak, and you can put links in a category by hand.

## ✨ Added

- **Free 1fichier links download without JDownloader.** The link collector shows their name, size and online state, and when 1fichier asks for a pause between free files, the task shows the wait and starts once it is over. Thanks to @selioss, whose report in [#155](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/155) started this.
- **Rapidgator, Keep2Share, FileBoom, TezFiles, Nitroflare and filer.net download on your premium login without JDownloader.** KnightLoader signs in through the hoster's API, fetches the file over several connections where the hoster allows it, and the login's row shows the plan, when it runs out and the traffic left.
- **Free Rapidgator, Keep2Share, FileBoom, TezFiles and filer.net links download without JDownloader.** KnightLoader sits out the countdown and asks for the captcha through the phone app and your captcha accounts.
- **ddownload, KatFile, Clicknupload, FileSpace and Uploadrar download free or on your login.** Their Turnstile captchas go to the phone app or a captcha account, and the wait between free downloads shows on the task.
- **Pixeldrain, Gofile and Mediafire links and folders download without JDownloader,** one row per file, subfolders included. A password-locked Gofile folder opens with the link password.
- **Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, SharePoint, WeTransfer and SwissTransfer shares download without JDownloader,** one row per file. Large Drive files get past the virus scan warning, and Google documents download as Word, Excel or PowerPoint files.
- **Krakenfiles, Workupload and Send.now links download for free without JDownloader.**
- **KnightLoader comes as a Flatpak for Linux,** for x64 and ARM, and the Apps page offers it next to Windows, macOS and Linux. Open it in your software center or run `flatpak install` on it.
- **The browser extension puts a download button on videos** on YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Twitch and Bilibili. One click sends the video you are watching to your instance and starts it, and with more than one instance online, the toolbar popup asks where the video goes. Thanks to @sabascos for the idea in [#169](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/169).
- **The video button has a card of its own in the extension's settings.** For each site you pick whether the button shows there, what a click downloads (video, audio, subtitles, thumbnail or the description) and the quality and format you prefer. Alt+Shift+K sends the video you are watching, and the card lets you change the shortcut.
- **The arrow next to the video button opens a card for each part of the video** with every quality and format it offers, each with its size and under its proper name, such as H.264, VP9, AAC or Opus, along with its audio languages and its subtitles as SRT, WebVTT or TTML. Audio can also come as MP3 or FLAC, a format KnightLoader converts to says so, and a quality at 60 fps or in HDR carries a small badge. The arrow can also send the whole playlist.
- **After a send, a ring around the video button's mark follows the download,** and "Done" opens your downloads. A video already in your list shows "Already there", and a pick that differs from it downloads as a row of its own. When a send fails, point at "Could not send" to see whether the relay could not be reached or your instance did not answer in time.
- **You can drag the video button anywhere on the player** or let it show only on hover. It follows your light or dark theme, turns gold under the pointer and lets a few stars fly when a video went through.
- **The thumbnail can come as JPG, PNG or WebP,** whatever format the site serves it in.
- **A video filmed in HDR offers its HDR tracks apart from the plain ones,** and a plain quality downloads the SDR track, where yt-dlp took the HDR one of the same height.
- **A video can be converted to H.265 in MKV.** It downloads at the quality you pick and is encoded again once it is there, and the row shows how far the conversion has got.
- **You can put links in a category by hand:** right-click a package or a selection in the collector or in Downloads and pick one under Category, or None to take them out. When you add links, Options has a Category field too, and a Packagizer rule that names a category still wins. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for asking how in [#158](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/158).
- **Each category can unpack into its own folder,** so all downloads can land in one temporary folder while series and films unpack where they belong. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for asking in [#158](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/158).
- **A Deepbrid premium account fetches torrents and `.nzb` files,** like TorBox and Premiumize.me. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for asking in [#157](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/157). It is built on Deepbrid's API documentation and not yet tried on a real account, so if something looks off, please tell us in the issue.
- **Well-known Usenet providers come as tiles.** Under Accounts, "Add a server" offers ten of them, Eweka and Newshosting among them, and "Other server" opens the empty form for any other provider. Pick yours and its server and encrypted port are filled in, along with the connection count where the provider states one, so only your login is left.

## 🎨 Design

- **KnightLoader has a redrawn logo,** in the web interface, the browser extension, the desktop app and the Android app.
- **KnightLoader follows GlimStone 4.3.1 everywhere,** and the Version card names it. Every selector keeps to one row: where its labels do not fit, it shows its glyphs alone, or turns into a dropdown if it has no glyphs. Under OLED the cards keep the dark theme's shadow, which still lifts a bubble or a menu off a card.
- **The sign-in page is GlimStone's sign-in card,** the same in every app of the family, with the logo large above the name and Sign in, the passkey and Forgot password? at full width. The code from the authenticator app and the reset form take their turn in the same card, and a refused try selects what was typed and shakes only its button. The language picker over the card is gone: the page speaks the language last chosen in this browser, or the browser's own.
- **While you hold an item to move it, every other item of the list trembles clearly,** so it is plain at once that they can be moved: the settings rail, the tabs, the overview's cards, the priority card, the download rows and the column heads, and the phone app's lists. Neighbours tremble out of step, and the download rows sway gently, since a full-width row would swing far at its ends.
- **Every list you reorder by hand places the moved item the same way,** so wide cards, long entries and a wide column such as Name reach both ends of their list. In the phone app a package with its files open can be moved to either end of the list as well.
- **A switch that refuses dims its track to half,** and on a touch screen its reason stands under the row.
- **Stop at the first matching rule is a switch like every other,** with its name at the start of the row and the switch at the end.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The Backend column shows who handles a download by its mark:** a debrid service's logo, a magnet for the built-in torrent client, and an icon each for JDownloader, yt-dlp, Usenet and direct downloads. Right-click the list header to switch it on. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for the idea in [#157](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/157).
- **The speed column shows how fast a debrid service fetches a torrent** while it is still downloading it to its own servers, and names the service when you point at it.
- **A login KnightLoader cannot use goes back to JDownloader,** and a download on its way moves on to the next backend instead of failing.
- **A hoster that asks for a browser check hands the download to JDownloader or a debrid service,** and the row says why.
- **The download priority order lists a hoster only once you connect it.**
- **Captchas always show** in the web interface and the phone app. The switch to turn them off is gone.
- **The test captcha can be a Turnstile, hCaptcha or reCAPTCHA check** as well as a picture.
- **Open folder sits at the top of a download's right-click menu.**
- **The Own servers card is called Seedboxes** and explains what it is for.
- **The password fields on the sign-in page show their name inside,** in grey, until you start typing.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **"Remove and delete files" takes the unpacked files along,** not only the archive, and the confirmation counts them in. "Remove" still keeps every file. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for the report in [#157](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/157).
- **A download JDownloader holds back for a hoster's cool-down waits instead of failing,** and the task shows JDownloader's wait and keeps following it. A task KnightLoader does give up on is switched off in JDownloader, so the two never disagree. Thanks to @selioss for the careful report with logs in [#155](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/155).
- **Stop works while downloads run.** It stayed greyed out for downloads that started on their own. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for the report in [#159](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/159).
- **The browser extension keeps its pairing in a Firefox that never remembers history or does not let it write to its database,** where the toolbar popup stayed empty or stopped before it showed your group. It puts the pairing in its own storage there. Thanks to @sabascos for the photos in [#169](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/169).
- **The Firefox extension loads without a warning,** since its manifest no longer asks for the offscreen permission that only Chromium has.
- **A page's own short sounds stay off "Media on this page"** in the extension, such as YouTube's voice-search sounds.
- **Rules can be edited and removed in the Graphic view.** Point at a rule or reach it with the keyboard, and a pencil and a bin appear right after its name. On a touch screen they stay in view.
- **The About text in the phone app no longer says the QR scanner sends diagnostics to Google.** The scanner reads the camera with ZXing and sends nothing anywhere, so the sentence was out of date in all 42 languages.
- **A video's quality pickers in the link collector offer only what the video has.**
- **A YouTube video set to 1080p shows the size of what yt-dlp downloads,** the same as "Best" where both fetch YouTube's Premium track. It showed the smaller size of another track.
- **A video wider than 16:9 names its qualities the way YouTube does,** so a 2:1 video offers its 1920x960 track as 1080p rather than 960p, and "Up to 1080p" on a 21:9 video no longer takes the 2560x1080 track that YouTube calls 1440p.
- **A video file carries the quality the menu showed,** so the 1080p track of a 2:1 video and a portrait 1080x1920 video both save as "(1080p)" instead of "(960p)" and "(1920p)", and their subtitles and thumbnail take the same name.
- **Subtitles picked as SRT or VTT come in that format from every site,** converted where the site serves another, and a TTML pick on a site without TTML keeps the site's own format and says so on the row.
- **A plain file behind a link without an extension downloads under its own name,** as one row, instead of going through yt-dlp as "(best).unknown_video".
- **A yt-dlp that starts slowly is still found.**
- **Open folder in the Windows desktop app shows the download's own folder,** also when the path holds a space, a comma or an `&`.
- **A second Linux desktop copy with its own data folder starts.**
- **Uninstalling the desktop app on Windows leaves nothing behind,** and the installer window shows KnightLoader's icon on Linux. The installer follows [PommelPorter 1.1.5](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/pommelporter/releases/tag/v1.1.5).
